stories.headline: Two trains crash into each other leaving 12 injured after 'signal failure' as emergency services rush to scene
stories.summary: Two trains collided head-on, resulting in 12 injuries, after a reported signal failure. Emergency services rushed to the scene to treat the injured. The incident is under investigation, with authorities considering all hypotheses, including a failure in the signalling system or human factors. The collision caused significant damage to the trains and sent broken glass flying. Four hundred passengers and staff were on board the two trains. The incident is the latest in a series of train crashes, with previous incidents highlighting concerns over signal failures and the safety of rail infrastructure. Investigators are working to determine the cause of the crash, with the safety director of the train operator confirming that several staff members were injured. The investigation is ongoing, with no official cause yet determined.

stories.headline: ‘Oreshnik’ Use Backfires On Putin By Exposing Russian Missile Tech - US Lawmaker
stories.summary: Russia used a hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missile in a mass attack on Kyiv, killing at least two people. This is only the third time Russia has used the Oreshnik missile, which is nuclear-capable. The attack, which also included drones, has raised concerns over the deployment of advanced weapons and fears of escalation. A US lawmaker noted that the use of the Oreshnik missile may backfire on Russia, as debris from the attack could provide Kyiv and Western analysts with valuable insights into the missile's capabilities. European leaders have condemned the attack, which is part of an intense assault on Ukraine. The use of the Oreshnik missile marks a rare and deadly strike on Ukraine, sparking renewed concerns over the conflict's trajectory.

stories.headline: Kremlin critics urge MPs to back bill that aims to strengthen sanctions law
stories.summary: Kremlin critics are testifying before MPs to urge support for a bill aimed at strengthening sanctions law. The bill has already passed the Federation Council and is expected to be signed into law by President Vladimir Putin. The legislation aims to restrict Russia's energy revenues and address sanctions evasion through third countries. US lawmakers, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune, have also expressed support for imposing tough sanctions on Russia. The EU has implemented sanctions on Russia since January 2025. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has stated that "all options are on the table" as the administration considers further sanctions on Russia. The bill's passage and potential signing into law mark a significant development in efforts to increase pressure on the Russian government.

stories.headline: US, Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire, begin nuclear talks
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative agreement to extend the ceasefire in the 3-month-old war by 60 days. The deal also paves the way for a new round of talks on Iran's nuclear program. According to a US official, the agreement is pending finalization, with US Vice President JD Vance stating that "a couple of language points" are still under discussion. Despite this, progress is being made in peace talks. Iranian officials have not yet commented on the potential deal. The extension of the ceasefire and the restart of nuclear talks mark a significant development in the conflict between the two nations, which has been ongoing for three months. The US official's announcement indicates a potential breakthrough in negotiations.

stories.headline: Call Of Duty: Warzone Joins Two Other Xbox One Games Being Delisted In Early June 2026
stories.summary: Call of Duty: Warzone will be delisted from Xbox One in early June 2026, along with two other Xbox One games. This means new downloads of the game will no longer be available. The decision comes as support for the game on last-gen consoles is ending, six years after its launch. The announcement coincides with the reveal of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which will not be released on Xbox One and PS4 when it launches in October. Existing players will still be able to play Warzone, but new players will not be able to download the game after the delisting. The exact date for the delisting is not specified, but it is expected to occur in early June 2026.

stories.headline: Apple working to cram massive Gemini model into iPhone to power new Siri
stories.summary: Apple is working to integrate Google's 1.2 trillion parameter Gemini artificial intelligence model into the iPhone to power a new version of Siri. The company has signed a multi-year deal with Google, estimated to be worth around $1 billion per year, to use the Gemini model. This partnership aims to enhance Siri's capabilities, making it smarter and more powerful. To achieve this, Apple is trying to shrink the massive Gemini model to fit into the iPhone, with a likely cloud component to support its functionality. The deal marks a significant shift in Apple's approach to artificial intelligence, leveraging Google's technology to improve its own intelligence features. The new Siri is expected to be part of upcoming iOS updates, including iOS 26.4 and iOS 27.

stories.headline: Magnon Breakthrough Could Shrink Quantum Computers to the Size of a Penny
stories.summary: An international team of physicists, led by Andrii Chumak from the University of Vienna, has achieved a major breakthrough in extending the lifetime of magnons. The team successfully measured magnon lifetimes of up to 18 microseconds, nearly 100 times longer than any previous observation. This significant advancement paves the way for the development of quantum computers that could be as small as a 1-cent coin. The extended magnon lifetime overcomes a key barrier to creating compact quantum computers and quantum sensing devices. The breakthrough could lead to the miniaturization of quantum computers, making them more accessible and potentially revolutionizing the field of quantum computing. The research team's findings have been reported, marking a substantial step forward in the development of smaller, more efficient quantum computers. This achievement is expected to have a significant impact on the future of quantum technology.

stories.headline: Listen: Experts sort quantum tech hype from reality
stories.summary: Quantum technology continues to attract significant investment from governments and tech companies, with the goal of building a supercomputer that can solve complex problems at unprecedented speeds. However, experts warn that exaggerated claims and hype surrounding quantum computing risk eroding public trust. Despite decades of research, quantum computing remains in its experimental stage, hindered by a lack of practical applicability. While it holds promise for revolutionary breakthroughs, it is still far from replacing classical systems. The near-term future is expected to be hybrid, with quantum and classical computing working together on niche, high-value applications. Companies are offering access to quantum hardware and simulators, allowing data science and R&D teams to conduct small-scale experiments and proof-of-concept projects, providing a low-risk way to gain practical experience with the technology. This hybrid approach is expected to drive progress in the field.

stories.headline: Iconic Isle of Man TT race cancelled as event sees 271st death and two-year-old airlifted to hospital
stories.summary: British rider Daniel Ingham, 33, has died following a crash during qualifying for the Isle of Man TT. The incident occurred at Doran's Bend on the western section of the course on Wednesday evening. Ingham's death marks the 271st fatality in the event's history. Additionally, a two-year-old child was airlifted to hospital, although the circumstances of this incident are unclear. The Isle of Man TT organizers have confirmed Ingham's death and released a statement. The event has now been cancelled due to the tragic incident. The Isle of Man TT is a prestigious motorcycle racing event known for its challenging course and high speeds, which has unfortunately led to numerous fatalities over the years.

stories.headline: Serena Williams Reportedly 'In Discussions' to Make Tennis Comeback, Full Details Revealed
stories.summary: Serena Williams, 44, is reportedly in discussions to make a comeback to professional tennis after nearly four years away from competitive sports. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion may return to the court in doubles with partner Victoria Mboko at Queen's Club in London, which takes place from June 8-14. This potential return comes four years after Williams unofficially retired from tennis. According to reports, Williams is pushing to participate in the doubles event, marking a significant development in her potential comeback. The news has sparked excitement among tennis fans, who have been awaiting Williams' return to the sport. If confirmed, Williams' participation at Queen's Club would be her first competitive tennis appearance in almost four years, raising anticipation for her possible return to singles competition.

stories.headline: Ombudsman sees off determined Gethin in thrilling Brigadier Gerard finish
stories.summary: Ombudsman won the Star Sports Brigadier Gerard Stakes at Sandown, narrowly defeating Gethin by a neck. The John and Thady Gosden-trained horse, a 2-5 favorite, was made to work hard by the runner-up. Ombudsman, a triple Group 1 winner, finished second in this race 12 months ago, beaten by Almaqam. Gethin, trained by Owen Burrows, was stepping up to Group 3 level after an impressive win in the Listed Magnolia Stakes at Kempton in April. Despite receiving seven pounds from Ombudsman, Gethin was unable to overcome the favorite, who went one place better than last year's result. The win was a narrow triumph for Ombudsman, who is considered a top contender ahead of Royal Ascot.

stories.headline: Osaka again catches the eye, Sabalenka marches on
stories.summary: Naomi Osaka made a statement at Roland-Garros with a sequined gold playing dress, drawing attention for her fashion choice. On the court, Osaka faced Donna Vekic, while Aryna Sabalenka advanced to the next round. Sabalenka had previously overcome a strong challenge from Osaka at the Madrid Open, coming from behind to win after Osaka took the opening set tie break. Sabalenka's class showed in the second set, which she won 6-3, taking the momentum away from Osaka and ultimately winning the deciding set. The temperature in Paris reached at least 32 degrees Celsius for the third consecutive day, adding to the challenge for players. Frenchwoman Lois Boisson, a surprise semifinalist last year, was eliminated from the tournament. Sabalenka, the World No 1, continued her progress as the clear favourite in the clay tournament.

stories.headline: Ajmer woman kills 4, burns bodies in SUV, then weeps with mourners after killing Police in Ajmer allege Sunita killed four family members and burnt their bodies inside a car to mimic an accident.
stories.summary: Police in Ajmer have arrested 45-year-old Sunita, the first wife of former sarpanch Ramsingh Chaudhary, in connection with the killings of four family members. The victims include Ramsingh, his mother, and two others. Sunita's 19-year-old daughter and 17-year-old son have been detained. Investigators allege that Sunita and her children loaded the bodies into a Scorpio SUV, took it to the highway, and set it ablaze to make the murders appear accidental. The incident occurred late Wednesday night. Sunita was seen pretending to cry with mourners, while her son was calm and drinking tea. Police suspect the killings were motivated by alleged torture by Ramsingh. The accused are being questioned, and further investigation is underway. The burning vehicle was found on the highway, and police are working to uncover the full circumstances of the crime.

stories.headline: At least 12 injured in clashes between rival groups in Haryana’s Nuh after Eid prayers
stories.summary: At least 12 people were injured in clashes between rival groups in Haryana's Nuh district following Eid al-Adha prayers. The violence erupted in two villages, where the groups pelted stones at each other and used sticks and axes, creating panic. The clashes are believed to have been sparked by old rivalries and disputes related to previous elections. Police intervened to restore order and are investigating the incident. The violence is a recurrence of a similar incident that occurred in Nuh's Tirwada village on March 21, where a longstanding rivalry led to a post-Eid prayer clash, resulting in several injuries. The latest incident has raised concerns and prompted police to take measures to prevent further escalation of the situation.

stories.headline: No legal action if infiltrators go back on their own: Amit Shah
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated that infiltrators who return to their countries voluntarily will not face legal action in India. He made this announcement during a public event in Gandhinagar, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation for various projects. Shah urged infiltrators to leave India on their own to avoid legal consequences. He also praised West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for handing over 600 hectares of land to the Border Security Force (BSF) for border fencing. Additionally, a committee has been formed to address demographic changes. The government's goal is to identify and deport infiltrators, and Shah's statement aims to encourage voluntary returns. This move is part of the government's efforts to address the issue of illegal immigration in the country.

stories.headline: A change in leadership in the three-year-old Karnataka government appears imminent, with Siddaramaiah having sought an appointment
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah is expected to step down from his post, reportedly after being asked by the Congress leadership to resign. This development comes despite Siddaramaiah's earlier statement that the Congress government would complete its full 5-year term. The three-year-old Karnataka government is on the verge of a leadership change, with DK Shivakumar likely to replace Siddaramaiah as the next Chief Minister. The Congress party has denied making any official decision on the leadership change. However, the Congress high command is pushing for a generational shift, leading to speculation about the imminent transition. Siddaramaiah had sought an appointment, fueling rumors about his potential resignation. The change in leadership is expected to take place soon, with Thursday being the speculated date for Siddaramaiah's resignation.

stories.headline: [Bangkok Post] Drama mixes with geopolitics in Cuba Admittedly, it looks a lot like a movie plot. A political thriller where the intelligence director of the chief adversary state comes into the nervous capital c
stories.summary: The US pressure campaign against Cuba has entered a new phase, with the country on the brink of collapse. The intelligence director of a chief adversary state recently met with Cuban regime leaders in the capital city, sparking speculation about the island's future. The outcome is uncertain, with possibilities ranging from economic change to comprehensive political reform or a supervised transitional state. Cubans have long lived in the shadow of the US, their superpower neighbor to the north. The country is facing significant challenges, with people rushing to complete daily tasks before sunset. The situation remains fluid, with the US playing a significant role in shaping Cuba's future, and the outcome of these developments is still unknown. The meeting between the intelligence director and Cuban leaders has added to the uncertainty and tension in the country.

stories.headline: [Free Press Journal] Marco Rubio's Kolkata Stop Signals A Recalibration In India-US Ties US Secretary of State Marco Rubio began his India visit in Kolkata, paying respects at Mother Teresa’s tomb before talks in New Delhi. The symbolic stop highlig
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio began his India visit in Kolkata, paying respects at Mother Teresa's tomb. He then proceeded to New Delhi for talks with Indian officials, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The visit aims to renew and strengthen ties between the two countries, with a focus on deeper energy cooperation. Rubio's stop in Kolkata was symbolic, highlighting the cultural and historical connections between the US and India. The visit comes ahead of Quad talks, a regional security dialogue between the US, India, Australia, and Japan. Rubio's meeting with Modi is expected to cover key issues, including energy, diplomacy, and trade, as the US seeks to recalibrate its relationship with India and promote mutual interests. The trip is part of the US effort to bolster its presence in the region and counterbalance other global powers.

These stories are part of the latest breaking news updates from around the world.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty rise on low oil price
stories.summary: Stock markets in India rose due to low oil prices. The Sensex and Nifty indices increased as crude oil prices decreased. This comes after a period of significant volatility in the market, triggered by surging oil prices that reached around $115 and $125 per barrel in recent months. The surge in oil prices was largely due to Middle East tensions, which added pressure to global markets. However, with oil prices now lower, the market has responded positively, with the Sensex and Nifty rising. The decrease in oil prices has eased some of the pressure on the market, leading to a increase in the key indices. The market had previously experienced sharp sell-offs, with the Nifty down around 600 points and the Sensex also plunging, but the current low oil price has helped to reverse this trend.

stories.headline: IT stocks lead gains as Sensex, Nifty open higher on easing oil prices
stories.summary: The S&P BSE Sensex rose 98.09 points to 75,965.89, and the NSE Nifty50 gained 16.20 points to 23,923.35, in early trade. IT stocks led the gains as the Indian stock market opened higher due to easing oil prices. This upward trend follows recent gains, including a surge of over 1,000 points in the Sensex and the Nifty closing above 24,000, driven by falling crude oil prices and strong buying in banking and IT sectors. The rupee has also strengthened, and broader indices are trading firmly in the green, despite valuation concerns. The rally is supported by buying in information technology stocks and eased volatility, contributing to the overall positive performance of the Indian stock market.

stories.headline: The S&P BSE Sensex rose 98.09 points, or 0.13%, to 75,965.89 in early trade, while the NSE Nifty50 gained 16.20 points, or 0.07%, to 23,923.35, as of 9:25 am
stories.summary: The S&P BSE Sensex rose 98.09 points to 75,965.89, a 0.13% increase, in early trade. The NSE Nifty50 gained 16.20 points to 23,923.35, a 0.07% increase, as of 9:25 am. This positive start is attributed to a drop in global crude oil prices. The market had seen a strong rally on Monday, with the Sensex and Nifty50 ending around 1.4% up due to supportive global cues. However, the previous day's trade saw the Nifty50 close at 23,907.15, down 7 points, and the Sensex end at 75,867.80, down 142 points. Analysts believe the indices need to move past the 23,800-23,900 zone to sustain the rally. The current gains indicate a continuation of the positive trend, with the market responding to global market sentiments and oil price fluctuations.

stories.headline: Anthropic finalises $65 billion funding deal, valuation surges past OpenAI to $965 billion
stories.summary: Anthropic has finalized a $65 billion funding deal, valuing the company at $965 billion. This surpasses OpenAI's valuation of $852 billion, making Anthropic the most valuable private AI company. The funding round, led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, has propelled Anthropic's valuation significantly. The company's Claude chatbot has driven rapid revenue and valuation growth. With this new valuation, Anthropic has leapfrogged OpenAI, which was last valued at $730 billion in a previous round and $852 billion post-money in March. The significant investment intensifies the competition between Anthropic and OpenAI in the rapidly evolving AI sector. The $965 billion valuation solidifies Anthropic's position as a leader in the industry.

stories.headline: Bitwise bets Hyperliquid could power future finance as HYPE ETFs gain traction
stories.summary: Bitwise has launched a Hyperliquid ETF, trading as BHYP on the NYSE, providing traditional investors with regulated access to the HYPE token. The ETF includes in-house staking, where some tokens are locked up to support the network and earn rewards. The Sponsor Fee is 0.34%, with a 0% fee for the first month on the Fund's first $500M. This launch comes as investor demand for Hyperliquid exposure surges, driven by a friendlier US regulatory environment. The HYPE token has climbed 21% since May 14. The Bitwise Hyperliquid ETF offers easy access to Hyperliquid without directly holding the token, supporting the high-performance Layer 1 blockchain built for on-chain trading and decentralized finance. The ETF is one of the first spot Hyperliquid exchange-traded products available in the US.

stories.headline: The Zscaler Sell-Off: Has the Market Overreacted?
stories.summary: Zscaler, Inc., a cloud security company, has experienced a significant sell-off, with its stock price down over 40% since the beginning of the year and 61% from its 52-week high of $336.99. The Nasdaq-listed company provides cybersecurity tools to protect enterprises from malicious websites, phishing emails, and other threats, including those targeting artificial intelligence applications. Despite its declining stock price, Zscaler's services remain crucial for enterprise network and data protection. The company has reported a net income of -$390.28 million. The substantial decline in stock price has raised questions about whether the market has overreacted, potentially making Zscaler a undervalued growth stock. With its cloud-based security solutions, Zscaler continues to play a vital role in the cybersecurity industry, prompting investors to reassess its stock value. The company's stock is currently trading at a significantly lower price than its recent peak.

stories.headline: Bank Of Africa Named Best Bank in North Africa at African Banker Awards 2026
stories.summary: Bank Of Africa (BOA) has been named Best Bank in North Africa at the 2026 African Banker Awards. The Moroccan banking group received the award in recognition of its performance in the region. This award is part of the annual African Banker Awards, which honor outstanding banks and financial institutions in Africa. The win for Bank Of Africa follows other recent awards in the banking sector, including the Euromoney Private Banking Awards and the International Banker Awards, which recognized various banks for their excellence in different categories. The African Banker Awards are a prestigious recognition of banks' achievements in the African financial sector. Bank Of Africa's win highlights its strong position in the North African banking market. The award ceremony took place as part of the annual African Banker Awards event.

stories.headline: Kate Conroy appointed inaugural general manager of Australian AI Safety Institute A philosopher and Royal Australian Air Force reservist has been chosen to lead the federal government's efforts to keep Australians safe from the harms of AI.
stories.summary: Kate Conroy has been appointed as the inaugural general manager of the Australian AI Safety Institute. A philosopher and Royal Australian Air Force reservist, Conroy co-authored a framework for governments using AI that became the national standard in 2024. She holds a PhD in philosophy and has worked at the University of Queensland and Queensland University of Technology. Conroy's appointment comes as Australia works to regulate AI, which is already integrated into various aspects of life. The Australian AI Safety Institute aims to keep Australians safe from the potential harms of AI. Conroy's experience and expertise will be crucial in establishing the institute and guiding the country's approach to AI safety. Her leadership will help shape Australia's regulatory efforts and ensure the responsible development and use of AI technology.

stories.headline: Elon Musk defends AI ambitions as IPO reveals trouble Elon Musk insists that his artificial intelligence venture xAI remains a serious competitor, pushing back against mounting doubts after revelations that the sup
stories.summary: Elon Musk is defending his artificial intelligence venture xAI, pushing back against mounting doubts after revelations from its IPO. Despite losing half of its founding members, including co-founders Jimmy Ba and Yuahai Wu, Musk insists xAI remains a serious competitor. He estimates that within 2 to 3 years, the lowest-cost way to generate AI compute will be in space, a prediction not shared by others. Musk's SpaceX is taking over xAI, unifying his business interests. xAI aims to compete with leading AI developers and integrate advanced AI capabilities into Musk's technology ecosystem. The company's ability to secure computing capacity is crucial, as AI firms constantly seek additional capacity from others. Musk's efforts to unify his businesses and expand xAI's capabilities come as the company faces challenges and doubts about its future.

stories.headline: Microsoft to release new coding model next week, the Information reports Microsoft is set to launch new artificial intelligence models next week at its Build conference. These include a coding model to enhance GitHub Copilot.
stories.summary: Microsoft is set to launch new artificial intelligence models at its Build conference next week. The models include a coding model to enhance GitHub Copilot, as well as models for transcription, reasoning, speech, and images. This move is part of Microsoft's strategy to reduce reliance on partners like OpenAI. The company plans to unveil the new models at its annual conference for developers in San Francisco. The coding model aims to boost the competitiveness of GitHub Copilot, a Microsoft-owned platform. The introduction of these homegrown AI models signals a shift towards greater self-sufficiency in AI technology for Microsoft. The company's shares saw a rise following the announcement, indicating positive market reception to the news. The Build conference will be a key platform for Microsoft to showcase its new AI capabilities and attract developer interest.
